world.h: UN warns Sudan's displaced may lose shelter
world.b: Two UN agencies say funding covers only about 10% of those in need as millions flee the war.
Ukraine wants specifics on how allied security support would work after the war, ahead of US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

world.h: Pope Leo begins Latin America tour
world.b: Three weeks after lung cancer surgery, the pope heads to Uruguay to start a trip that also takes in Argentina and Peru through Nov. 17.

world.h: Trump says US is talking to Tehran's representatives
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage of the US-Israel war on Iran.
world.title: Trump says US talking to Tehran’s representatives, says ‘doing very well’

national.h: Cornell faculty vote no confidence in leaders
national.b: The Faculty Senate passed the symbolic resolution 75-50 after a former student sued, saying she was gang raped at a fraternity party in 2024.
national.title: Cornell faculty vote ‘no confidence’ in university leadership after alleged fraternity gang rape

national.b: Schools already shrinking from low birth rates are losing immigrant children, and Los Angeles officials say campuses will likely have to close.

politics.h: Arizona Democrats win first trifecta since 1966
politics.b: Democrats took both legislative chambers and kept the governor's office. Gov. Katie Hobbs vetoed more than 540 Republican bills in her first term.
politics.title: Democrats win the Arizona House, Senate and governor’s office for the first time since 1966

politics.h: Sen. Chris Murphy leaves hospital after stroke
politics.b: The Connecticut Democrat will miss several weeks of Senate votes while he recovers in a rehabilitation facility.

politics.h: Mississippi Senate race still too close to call
politics.b: Fewer than 2,000 votes separate Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom, and no one can say how many ballots remain.
politics.title: No one knows how many ballots are outstanding in Mississippi's Senate race

politics.h: Schumer vows to block a 'right-winger' on Supreme Court
politics.b: The Senate Democratic leader said his party won't confirm 'crappy nominees' to the courts or Cabinet once it takes power.

politics.h: Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff
politics.b: Trump said Miller will replace Susie Wiles days after Republicans lost Congress. Wiles will keep working for his political organization.
politics.title: Trump names Stephen Miller his next chief of staff after major Republican midterm losses

politics.h: Harmeet Dhillon resigns from Justice Department
politics.b: The assistant attorney general oversaw a sweeping reshaping of the Civil Rights Division, including mass departures of career lawyers.

politics.h: Trump says he is willing to work with Democrats
politics.b: 'I don't want to be just sitting there for two years just vetoing everything,' he said, as Democrats hold comfortable majorities in both chambers.

politics.h: Burgum pushes public-land data centers while invested in AI
politics.b: ProPublica reports the interior secretary, who is leading the push to put data centers on federal land, has tens of millions invested in the AI industry.
politics.title: Trump Official Who Wants Data Centers on Public Lands Has Tens of Millions Invested in AI Industry

international.h: Protesters occupy Amsterdam Microsoft data centre site
international.b: Demonstrators broke into the construction site trying to stop the project, and police were removing them by late afternoon.
international.title: Protesters break into Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam

international.h: Armed men kill 33 in eastern Congo village
international.b: Officials blamed the ADF armed group, whose fighters also set fire to more than 50 houses near Beni.
Lawmakers filed charges against the president despite his resignation, after a 78-0 lower house vote amid a bank collapse crisis.
international.title: Paraguay resumes Pena impeachment proceedings as financial crisis deepens

international.h: Strikes on Taiz market kill civilians
international.b: The Houthis say Saudi air strikes killed at least 30 civilians at the Yemeni market; government forces and the Houthis blame each other.
international.title: Yemeni gov’t forces, Houthis trade blame for deadly strikes on Taiz market

international.b: Ireland's RTE briefly evacuated staff in Dublin after an emailed threat, and Bulgaria's Nova TV was also targeted, after a week of hoaxes against flights.
Rescuers recovered eight more bodies in Komyshuvakha, and the acting regional governor put the toll at 53 after Monday's Russian strike.

international.h: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years
international.b: Paul Mackenzie's sect ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to death. Twenty-eight accomplices were also jailed.

business.h: US urges China to honour Busan trade deal
business.b: The Treasury announced talks on the deal in which Trump and Xi agreed to ease tariffs and tech restrictions. China says it may buy more US farm goods.
business.title: US urges China to honour Busan trade deal commitments

business.h: US employers add 165,000 jobs in October
business.b: Unemployment dipped to 4.1% and wages rose 3.1% from a year ago. Health care and manufacturing added jobs while restaurants and construction cut them.

science.h: Tomb finds point to cannabis high 2,800 years ago
science.b: Seeds and hair from a Siberian tomb suggest psychoactive cannabis use at least 300 years earlier than known use in China.
science.title: Seeds and preserved hair in tomb point to oldest signs of cannabis high 2,800 years ago, study suggests

sports.h: Prescott unsure Cowboys are proud of offense
sports.b: Dak Prescott said 'we'll be better, I can promise' as Dallas ranks near the bottom in motion and play action at midseason.
Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb pushed back on talk of trading the franchise-tagged receiver ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

sports.h: No. 1 Miami visits No. 11 Notre Dame
sports.b: The Irish get a shot at revenge for the Week 1 loss that kept them out of last year's playoff.

sports.h: NBA weighs shortening games to 40 minutes
sports.b: Commissioner Adam Silver has backed four 10-minute quarters as the league battles an injury crisis.

local.h: Queens driver indicted in stroller crash that killed baby
local.b: Prosecutors say Elvin Rivera ran a stop sign in Flushing on cocaine and THC and struck 1-year-old Justin Hu.
local.title: Intoxicated Queens driver killed baby after running stop sign, indictment says

local.h: Penn Station plan could fund a new MSG venue
local.b: Amtrak's overhaul would buy and demolish the Infosys Theater, and MSG says sale money could pay for a new venue.
local.title: Amtrak's Penn Station plan could funnel taxpayer money to new venue for James Dolan

local.h: Google, NYC schools clash over AI ban
local.b: Google said schools that ban AI will lose access to its search, and Mayor Mamdani accused it of using monopoly power to force AI into classrooms.
local.title: NYC schools’ standoff with Google over AI raises prospect of no search in class

local.h: Supreme Court case could limit specialized school reforms
local.b: Experts say a challenge to a Maryland county's magnet school admissions could narrow Mayor Mamdani's options for admitting more Black and Latino students.
local.title: Supreme Court case could affect admissions reforms for NYC specialized schools

local.h: Two found shot dead at East Harlem senior center
local.b: Police found a 55-year-old woman and a 66-year-old man at a NYCHA complex Thursday night and are investigating whether it was a murder-suicide.
local.title: Health aide, elderly man killed in East Harlem senior center shooting, per NYPD

local.h: South Bronx, East New York lead in low-level tickets
local.b: A John Jay College analysis found more than 60% of NYPD loitering summonses since 2025 came from one South Bronx precinct.
local.title: South Bronx, East New York lead NYC in littering and panhandling tickets, analysis finds
